Keyence from Neutral to Buy, THK from Sell to Neutral, SMC from Buy to Neutral

In light of the January–March quarter results and the FA industry demand trends that have become more apparent recently, we have significantly revised our forecasts and the premiums for calculating 12-month target prices for FA companies in our coverage. The tightness in supply/demand and the accompanying changes in order trends have been significant. We believe many companies will achieve record-high profits through FY3/28E, and a growing number of companies will achieve this as early as FY3/27E. Given that a new peak cycle has begun, and given that the direction of capital allocation policies — a major focus area for investors — has become clearer for companies post recent results, we broadly revise our forecasts and applied multiples for companies in our coverage. We incorporate recent results and adjust estimates for latest trends for our coverage universe, with 12m TPs changing for 9 stocks by -11% to +44%: Okuma from ¥3,700 to ¥3,800, THK from ¥5,200 to ¥7,500, Misumi from ¥3,400 to ¥3,500, SMC from ¥90,000 to ¥80,000, Daifuku from ¥8,600 to ¥9,300, Yaskawa Electric from ¥7,300 to ¥9,200, Omron from ¥6,500 to ¥7,400, Keyence from ¥82,000 to ¥100,000, and Fanuc from ¥5,300 to ¥5,600. Based on the updated sector relative valuation, we upgrade Keyence from Neutral to Buy (company’s competitive moat to benefit within a tight supply/demand environment + we expect expansion of capital allocation policies), THK from Sell to Neutral (benefits from tight supply/demand are likely to more than offset challenges from intensifying competition), and downgrade SMC from Buy to Neutral (fundamentals remain strong but uncertainty over margins/ROC/capital allocation policies to weigh on valuations).

AI Capex is likely to continue for the time being; we expect yoy momentum to peak in FY3/27E to FY3/28E

Multiple companies have mentioned at earnings presentations and elsewhere that April order trends or recent inquiries are at record-high levels, suggesting that activity is at an intense level comparable to the past peak cycles of CY2021–22 and CY2017–18. The most prominent example is arguably Japan Machine Tool Builders' Association's March–April order data, which unexpectedly set new all-time monthly highs, centered in Asia/America. We believe this is driven by the strength of AI Capex demand expanding from semiconductors at the forefront to batteries, servers, and their peripheral components, with benefits extending beyond tech/electronics equipment to general industrial machinery as well. This trend has become more pronounced since the Lunar New Year and appears to have accelerated from April onward. We believe as long as the acceleration in core AI Capex areas, led by semiconductors, remains strong, this trend is likely to continue in the near future.

Our global tech team expects semiconductor capex growth of +29% in CY26 / +17% in CY27 / +3% in CY28, and WFE growth of +28% in CY26 / +32% in CY27 / +12% in CY28, projecting a high growth trajectory through at least CY27 (link). In addition, we forecast that industrial machinery, represented by machine tools, will remain reasonably strong through FY3/27, centered on China. In particular, the benefits of the broadening of AI Capex, primarily in China, are manifesting as upside to orders, and we reiterate our forecast FY3/27 at ¥1.9 trillion (+11.5% YoY) and FY3/28 at ¥1.8 trillion (-5.3% YoY). We expect the peak to be marked in FY3/27.

Whether or not companies possess supply capacity will become the focus point

We reiterate our view that the greater focal point going forward for the FA industry and capital markets will not be demand trends but rather the presence or absence of supply capacity. This is because, in response to demand trends that are rising vertically, supply tightness has in turn become the biggest problem. In semiconductor-related areas, procurement of components for some FA equipment has been seeing some challenges (starting with semiconductor memory and most recently extending to general-purpose ICs). Additionally, as an effect of the macro environment changes stemming from the Middle East situation, procurement difficulties for petrochemical products such as paints and oils have led to advance ordering on the raw materials side emerging early on. The same trend can be seen on the FA equipment side as well, and among some FA product categories — for example, in metal-processed components — ball screws appear to be tightening early on. We believe the trend of advance orders accumulating also needs to be closely watched. During the peak cycle of CY17, approximately ten years ago, supply-demand tightness — triggered by semiconductor memory in the electronics segment and intense demand growth from China in the FA segment — led to overlapping advance orders that amplified the sharp acceleration in momentum. As excessive orders piled up and lead times extended, the tendency toward advance ordering and double ordering intensified further, and in some cases, changeovers and rush orders also overlapped, leading to rising manufacturing fixed costs and labor costs. Whether companies can avoid repeating that pattern — through their ability to maintain strong procurement networks, strong production systems, and proper discipline on lead times and pricing — will be an important fact to watch going forward.
Our Forecasts and Views: Incorporating near-term earnings upside, broadly raising target prices

Primarily driven by a revision of demand assumptions — in particular, the bringing forward of the timing of the peak in momentum to FY3/27 through FY3/28 as described above — we have revised our operating profit forecasts from this fiscal year onward by an average of 2–4%. For Okuma, Omron, and CKD, we introduce our FY3/29 forecasts with this report.
Our operating profit forecasts for FY3/27 through FY3/28 are around 10% above IBES consensus estimates, despite the fact the consensus has already been rising lately on

strong near-term earnings delivery in March quarter. We believe this is because, as described above, record-high or near-record order trends and strong profit generation driven by operating leverage can be expected as early as 1Q of FY3/27. As it is reconfirmed that order upside translates firmly into earnings upside, we expect further share price re-rating.

Regarding our 12-month target prices, for most stocks we have raised them in line with our upward earnings revisions. In addition to the above, recent earnings trends and shifts in the operating environment have also prompted us to revise valuation multiple premiums and investment ratings across a number of names. For Yaskawa Electric, the multiple premium has been revised from +60% to +90%; for Keyence, from +140% to +170%; for THK, from ±0% to +40%; and for SMC, from +50% to +20%. Fanuc is the sole exception where our investment thesis remains unchanged; however, given the sharp recent re-rating of its trading multiple, we have revised our sector-relative multiple assumption from +60% to +70%.

While we see no significant changes to the fundamental risks to our estimates and TPs for FA companies in our coverage, we believe their positioning in terms of supply capacity is likely to be a major focus point in this cycle. We maintain our bullish view on the FA sub-sector.

Given the favorable and buoyant operating environment, we expect early achievement of the company's already-announced medium-term plan targets (link). We expect high likelihood of updates on its target at the management briefing and new plant tour scheduled for June 1 at the company's headquarters, and that upside in order trends and earnings will likely be confirmed early on at the 1Q results announcement expected in early July. Our operating profit estimates remain \(10 - 20\%\) above I/B/E/S consensus, and we see upside risks to consensus estimates.

We expect Yaskawa to be a key beneficiary from the expansion of AI capex driven by a tightening supply-demand balance in the MC business (link). In addition to servo motors, where demand remains strong for semiconductor production equipment and for industrial machinery serving the electronics industry as AI capex broadens demand, North American inverter demand has also been strong. With the company capturing AI capex demand broadly, including HVAC demand for data centers and energy demand (for oil and gas), which can be considered indirect AI demand, we remain positive on the company's positioning.

We expect the company to achieve record-high profits, driven by the MC businesses, the mainstay driver for the company where AI Capex inquiries are currently the strongest. We raise our FY2/27 operating profit estimate to ¥73.0 bn from ¥70.0 bn. We maintain our FY2/28 onward estimates, and our FY2/27-FY2/29 estimates are +12%/+18%/+21% above I/B/E/S consensus.

We raise our 12-month target price to ¥9,200 from ¥7,300. We expect record-high profits driven by the MC business, a return of company-wide capital return metrics (such as ROE and CROCI) to near historical highs, and record-high OPM in the MC business to push the stock's multiple higher to the same level as past peak cycles. We raise the premium used in our target price calculation to 90% from 60%, to the same level as
FY2/18, when the company's profitability was strong, driven primarily by the MC business.

We believe the company is approaching an inflection point in terms of both fundamentals and valuation after a period of subdued performance. In terms of fundamentals, we see operating leverage kicking in with semiconductors and AI Capex driving top-line growth, increased production, and improved utilization, and we believe this will set up an earnings recovery exceeding consensus expectations from FY2/27 onward driven by its mainstay MC businesses.

We believe Yaskawa Electric is entering a phase of meaningful earnings acceleration, underpinned by structural tailwinds from the expanding AI capital expenditure cycle. Recent demand trends reinforce our conviction in this inflection point. With historical peak margins and returns on invested capital now recovering, we expect the stock's valuation premium to re-rate toward prior-cycle highs. We reiterate our Buy rating.

Investor expectations had been building ahead of the full-year results that Keyence would become more proactive on shareholder returns and disclosures. We believe these expectations were duly met by the announcement of improved disclosure and a change to the articles of incorporation to enable share buybacks. The scale of the new capital policy, including share buybacks, will continue to attract investor attention, in our view. In addition, there are growing opportunities for the stock to be re-evaluated on fundamentals. In the current buoyant environment where supply-demand tightness is in focus, we expect investors to increasingly focus on Keyence's supply structure and business model, which enables it to capture emerging FA demand by maintaining a stable supply framework. We raise our estimates and target price, and upgrade our rating from Neutral to Buy.

As evidenced by the strong momentum in orders across FA companies, we believe the key focus going forward would be whether companies can continue to fulfill their supply responsibilities smoothly and reliably in an environment where advance ordering is intensifying across the FA industry and delivery lead-time issues could emerge. Also, whether companies can achieve higher prices/mix in response to supply-demand tightness. We think this will be the most important factor in assessing the earnings outlook, and we believe Keyence's business model (same-day delivery model, minimal manufacturing burden, optimal portfolio/service structure, etc.) is well positioned to leverage this inflection. In light of the current demand environment, and assuming that Keyence's pricing/mix will benefit from further improvement opportunities under current conditions, we raise our OP estimates for FY3/27E-FY3/29E by +8%-+23%. We now forecast the gross margin to average above 83% and the operating margin to be maintained consistently above 51%.

We also expect the series of initiatives by Keyence's management, particularly its proactive stance on capital returns and disclosures to continue. On shareholder returns, we believe the company's focus has shifted towards adjusting future cash allocation than
to return the cash it currently holds. Accordingly, we assume a total shareholder return payout ratio of around 60-70% and have factored this into our estimates.

Our 12-month target price is ¥100,000 (previously ¥82,000). We change the basis year for our target price calculation to FY3/28E from the average of FY3/27E-FY3/28E, in line with other FA stocks, and raise the sector-relative premium to 170% from 140%. We believe given Keyence's position to benefit from AI Capex demand, it warrants valuation levels closer to its historical highs when it recorded highest returns, profitability, and growth within its peers. With 27% upside potential to our new 12m TP (vs. 15% avg. upside for our Japan FA coverage), we upgrade our rating to Buy.

A capital policy enhancement that falls short of our expectations or capital market expectations. We currently estimate that a total shareholder return payout ratio of 60-70%, equivalent to over ¥200 bn/year in share buybacks, is a level that can be achieved without significantly changing the company's balance sheet composition. If the actual level falls well short of this, or if no announcement is made at all, it could be a negative surprise.

A downturn in fundamentals well below our expectations. We expect Keyence's business model to increasingly stand out in the current environment, where supply-demand conditions are particularly tight. Its supply chain strength and ability to deliver products immediately should give it a strong competitive edge in the current environment. If the company is unable to leverage this competitive edge and sales growth comes under pressure, this would pose a significant downside versus our expectations.

A decline in margins due to higher variable and fixed costs, particularly a miss on \(50\%\) OPM. We expect investor focus to remain on Keyence's competitive advantage and its ability to maintain strong profitability each quarter. While the gross margin has remained above \(80\%\), the share price reaction to past quarters when OPM fell below \(50\%\) is a case in point, a decline in OPM below our expectation would pose downside risks to our estimates and TP.

We are Buy-rated on Keyence. Keyence is an unrivaled player in the global factory automation space, providing high value-add that exceeds offerings of its peers. With its differentiated business model with short delivery times and consulting/sales offerings supported by its high value-add per worker and fast and flexible product development capabilities to meet customers' needs, we believe the company has a well established competitive moat. The company has achieved higher returns and margins relative to the global capital goods and factory automation sectors. However, we believe the current valuation premium (below historical median) relative to the sector, is not factoring in this fully. Key catalysts for re-rating: Company's initiatives to improve capital efficiency.

We have been cautious on THK's business environment, particularly the risk of intensifying competition and market share erosion, mainly in the China business. However, the strength of current demand has reached peak levels seen over the past decade, with AI Capex demand expanding not only to semiconductors but across a broad range of industrial machinery, and as a result, order upside has significantly exceeded our assumptions. The sharp rise in manufacturing costs that is likely to emerge going forward also appears likely to be smoothly offset by price hike initiatives backed by tight supply/demand conditions. As a result, we revise our estimates and also raise our valuation premium from the previous 0% to 40% (the current spot level is 60%), the average since November 2024 when the company renewed its capital policy. Our new target price is ¥7,500 (from¥5,200), and we upgrade our rating from Sell to Neutral on a sector relative basis.
Since downgrading the stock to Sell on 22 April 2022, the stock's has been up \(101\%\) (TOPIX \(110\%\)).

The key point of focus going forward will be whether the company can smoothly achieve sales growth and the accompanying profit growth. Although there is some unevenness depending on the product, we feel that the current surge in demand is comparable to the rapid rise in FA demand seen in 2016-2018. Supply tightness risks are already emerging for some products, and concerns about rising material costs and procurement uncertainties stemming from the situation in the Middle East are adding to this. The risk of rising variable costs overall, mainly raw material costs, appears unavoidable. We believe price pass-through will also be inevitable, but the focus will be on whether the company can pass through more than the corresponding amount of cost increases. Furthermore, if pre-orders and double-ordering risks emerge as in past cycles, the focus is likely to shift to topics such as whether the order backlog is healthy. We will continue to monitor the company's ability to maintain discipline in managing orders.

Our estimates incorporate some improvement in sales prices/product mix, and assume that excessive order upside/production upside, and increase of cost will not occur for the time being. Given that production appetite in the semiconductor manufacturing equipment industry, a key end-market, is expected to remain reasonably strong through around mid-2027, we expect elevated earnings levels to continue through the end of 2027. Whether the company's earnings subsequently peak out will likely hinge on whether it can avoid challenges as seen in past cycles — namely, the company had taken excessive advance orders and as a result faced operational issues.

Our 12-month target price is revised from ¥5,200 to ¥7,500, based on a sector-appropriate EV/EBITDA multiple of 10X and a sector-relative premium revised from 0% to 40%. The basis for the 40% premium is as noted above, the average from the announcement of the new capital policy in November 2024 to current levels (the current spot level is over 60%). With 0% upside to our revised 12m TP (vs. 15% avg. upside for our Japan FA coverage), we upgrade our rating from Sell to Neutral.

Changes in sales price trends and raw material costs beyond our assumptions. Linear motion components, which are metal-fabricated products, have historically seen significant earnings swings driven by large fluctuations in variable cost trends and sales price trends. As supply/demand tightness has become pronounced again in this cycle, attention is likely to focus on sales price trends and variable cost trends. Any material changes vs our assumptions would pose risks to out estimates/TP.
Distribution inventory trends (excess vs. shortage) and lead time trends

(lengthening/shortening) as indicators of supply/demand tightness. As these are metal-fabricated products, it is difficult to shorten lead times rapidly, and lead times tend to lengthen when supply/demand is tight. As a result, customers have historically placed pre-orders and double orders. Cyclicality could be amplified if such events occur. Accordingly, the strength/weakness of near-term earnings may be overstated relative to the underlying fundamentals.
Market share trends in the China market and global markets. We view the

intensification of competition as an irreversible trend, led by Hengli in the China market and Hiwin in the global market. Given the current demand strength, all players appear to be benefiting for the time being, but once the supply/demand balance normalizes, competition for market share is likely to intensify again.

Our Buy rating on SMC has been driven by sharp earnings recovery driven by operating leverage, given that it has the third-highest profit contribution from the semiconductor field among our FA coverage names and has been expanding production capacity. Indeed, in its FY3/26 4Q results, SMC announced an earnings beat, an orders beat, and guidance that, while conservative, was in line with consensus expectations, along with a ¥50 bn share buyback. However, the stock price decline post results likely driven by the cancellation of the anticipated capital allocation policy announcement and medium-term vision. A new management structure was also announced, and at the briefing on May 14, President Takada Yoshiki emphasized that the company intends to prioritize its core business growth strategy for the time being. Comments on the new capital allocation policy and medium-term vision highlighted that the company would consider whether to announce these after the new management team is in place.

In addition to the sharp earnings recovery following the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, the sector-relative premium assigned to SMC's stock had risen to levels comparable with other FA companies, thanks in part to proactive capital returns policy announcement by the company. This was likely a reflection of not only of expectations for high profitability and growth, but also of investors pricing in expectations that the company's cash management would move in a positive direction. Despite favorable earnings trends, the decline in the share price after latest results highlights potential investor concerns around the company's capital returns policy going forward. Our previous valuation multiple premium was derived from the five-year average sector-relative premium covering the period from the post-COVID earnings recovery and proactive capital market engagement through to the present. With this report, we have recalibrated the premium using a longer historical window of over ten years, incorporating the period prior to that recovery phase. As a result, we are reducing our sector-relative multiple premium from +50% to +20%. Consequently, our 12-month target price is revised downward from ¥90,000 to ¥80,000. We downgrade our rating from Buy to Neutral

based on relative upside within our coverage. Since upgrading the stock to Buy on 21 February 2019, the share price has increased by 72% vs TOPIX 144%. While there were periods in which strong earnings growth and proactive disclosure improvements were well received by the market, the primary driver of underperformance was, in our view, the failure to meet capital market expectations sufficient to sustain multiple expansion — most notably with respect to capital allocation policy and shareholder returns.

SMC's disclosed fundamentals point to an upturn, as evidenced by strong order trends. Given its position as the world's No. 1 pneumatics manufacturer and strong demand in high value-added areas where it has high market share, led by semiconductors, we continue to expect significant upside to FY3/26 earnings. Although it is necessary to factor in some increase in manufacturing-related costs, as the company itself has noted, we believe the increase in marginal profits from higher volume will more than offset the negatives. In light of the strong demand environment that has become evident, we revise our operating profit estimates by -5% to +6%. We raise our near-term FY3/27 estimate while lowering our estimates through FY3/29, mainly because some customers are increasingly pushing for aggressive pull-forward of orders. We expect SMC's earnings strength to be particularly pronounced from FY3/27 through FY3/28.

On the other hand, it is unclear whether there will be any update on capital allocation policy. While we believe any positive update from the company on its capital returns policy could be seen positively by investors, given SMC's comments that it wants to focus for the time being on how to strengthen top-line growth and actively explore possibilities such as M&A, we expect near-term overhang on share price to remain.

However, we believe the strength of its fundamentals and its decline YTD, provides valuation support. With our 12m TP of SMC implying 20% upside (vs. 15% avg. for Japan FA coverage) and lack of near-term catalysts, we downgrade the stock to Neutral from Buy.

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
